LFP Compression Benchmark: SVD and Adaptive SVD+WP Methods

electrophysiology
LFP
compression
Neuropixels
Benchmarking SVD-based LFP compression methods on 11 Neuropixels insertions, evaluating RMSE and SNR across compression ratios up to 3000×.
Author

Olivier Winter

Published

June 9, 2026

Overview

The IBL holds 936 hours of Brainwide Map (BWM) recordings and 1472 hours from the Ephys Atlas. Raw LFP at 2500 Hz, 384 channels, float32 amounts to ~12 TB for the BWM alone. After standard preprocessing (bad-channel rejection, 2–250 Hz bandpass, ×10 decimation to 250 Hz), the footprint shrinks to ~1.2 Tb — still too large for routine distribution or streaming. The goal is to identify a lossy compression strategy that reduces this further.

Practical recommendation: SVD-adapt-CR32-WP4. Setting the SVD stage to CR≈32 (rank≈12, epsilon≈48) and WP keep_frac ≈ 0.25 gives a total CR≈128 with SNR > 10 dB. This would shrink the dataset to ~9.6 Gb.

Pre-processing pipeline

Raw LFP (NP1, 2500 Hz, .cbin) was preprocessed before benchmarking:

  1. Bad-channel detection — channels with anomalous variance flagged and excluded.
  2. Bandpass + CAR + decimation — 2–250 Hz FIR bandpass, common-average referencing, ×10 FIR decimation → 250 Hz float32.
  3. Cadzow PPCA spatial denoising — F-X Cadzow on 3 s snippets (nw=64, f_max=100 Hz, max rank r=5, adaptive rank via singular-value gap threshold=2.0, PPCA outlier k=2.0) to remove incoherent channel noise.

All methods were benchmarked on the Cadzow-denoised snippets so residuals reflect compression loss, not pre-existing noise.

Compression methods

Method Principle CR formula Sweep
SVD Truncated SVD of the nc×ns matrix; store the top-r singular triplets. Exploits spatial correlations across channels. nc·ns / (r·(nc+ns)) r ∈ {1,2,4,8,16,32,64,96}
SVD-adapt SVD with adaptive rank selection: retain singular values where \(s_k > \varepsilon \cdot \sigma_0\), with \(\sigma_0 = \text{median}(\text{lower half of } s)\) as the noise-floor estimate. \(\varepsilon\) is a dimensionless multiplier — equivalently, the minimum signal-to-noise-floor ratio \(s_k / \sigma_0\) required to keep a component. \(\varepsilon\) is swept to cover a wide CR range. nc·ns / (r_adapt·(nc+ns)) ε ∈ logspace(10⁴, 10⁻¹, 30)
SVD-adapt-CR24-WP Two-stage: SVD at rank→CR≈24, then db4 wavelet-packet thresholding on the r temporal rows of Vh. CR24 / f f ∈ {0.005…0.50}
SVD-adapt-CR32-WP As above, SVD stage targeting CR≈32. CR32 / f f ∈ {0.005…0.50}
SVD-adapt-CR48-WP As above, SVD stage targeting CR≈48. CR48 / f f ∈ {0.005…0.50}

Metrics

\[\text{RMSE}(c) = \left\langle \sqrt{\left\langle (x - \hat{x})^2 \right\rangle_t} \right\rangle_{\text{snippets}} \quad [\mu\text{V}] \qquad \text{SNR}(c) = 20 \cdot \log_{10} \left( \frac{\text{RMS}(c)}{\text{RMSE}(c)} \right) \quad [\text{dB}]\]

Aggregated as median over channels, then mean over 11 PIDs.

Results

Aggregate benchmark (11 PIDs)

SVD and SVD-adapt (ε-sweep) track each other closely — the noise-floor threshold recovers the same ranks as the fixed sweep and is fully automatic. All SVD-adapt-WP variants extend usable CR well beyond the pure SVD plateau; lower initial CR (tighter SVD stage) generally delivers better quality at any given combined CR.

Reconstruction and residual galleries

SVD and SVD-adapt retain coherent spatial structure to CR=100; WP variants extend clean reconstruction to CR=300–1000.

SVD/SVD-adapt residuals are spatially incoherent across all CRs. SVD-adapt-WP residuals show mild wavelet-domain artefacts at extreme CRs (> 300×).

SVD spectrum and ε calibration

Median ε values (and range across 11 PIDs) that select each evaluated rank:

Rank ε median ε range
1 4073 2772–4697
2 2252 1540–2898
4 909 574–1240
8 461 255–584
16 155 89–207
32 47 22–73
64 10 4–22
96 4 1–10

Conclusions

  • SVD-adapt (ε-sweep) matches plain SVD quality: noise-floor threshold recovers the same ranks as the manual sweep and is fully automatic.
  • Visually all compressions degrade above CR128

NoteSVD-adapt-WP algorithm in detail

The two-stage algorithm operates on a snippet matrix \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{n_c \times n_s}\) (channels × samples):

Stage 1 — spatial compression (SVD)

\[X \approx \hat{X}_1 = U_r \, \text{diag}(s_r) \, V_r^\top\]

where \(U_r \in \mathbb{R}^{n_c \times r}\), \(s_r \in \mathbb{R}^r\), \(V_r^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times n_s}\) are the top-\(r\) singular triplets. The rank \(r\) is chosen to achieve a target CR (e.g. CR=24 → \(r \approx 12\)).

Stage 2 — temporal compression (wavelet packets)

Each of the \(r\) rows of \(V_r^\top\) is independently compressed using db4 wavelet packet decomposition (level 5). Only the top-\(f\) fraction of coefficients by magnitude are retained, giving an overall:

\[\text{CR}_{\text{total}} = \frac{n_c \, n_s}{r(n_c + n_s)} \cdot \frac{1}{f}\]

SVD-adapt (ε-sweep) selects rank automatically using:

\[\sigma_0 = \text{median}(s_{\lfloor r/2 \rfloor + 1}, \ldots, s_r), \qquad r^* = \max\{k : s_k > \varepsilon \cdot \sigma_0\}\]

Here \(\sigma_0\) is the noise-floor estimate (median of the lower half of the full singular value spectrum), and \(\varepsilon\) is a dimensionless threshold — the minimum signal-to-noise-floor ratio \(s_k / \sigma_0\) required to retain a component. Equivalently, \(\varepsilon(r) = s_r / \sigma_0\) is the \(\varepsilon\) that would select exactly rank \(r\) (as shown in the calibration figure). Sweeping \(\varepsilon\) from \(10^4\) (keep only the dominant component) down to \(10^{-1}\) (keep almost everything) traces out the full CR curve.

Reconstruction reverses the two stages: reconstruct each wavelet-compressed row, then reassemble \(\hat{X} = U_r \, \text{diag}(s_r) \, \hat{V}_r^\top\).

NotePrior context: transform methods

Before focusing on SVD variants, we benchmarked six approaches: SVD, Wavelet Packets (WP), DCT, DCT-δ, STFT, and SVD+WP. SVD consistently outperformed all transform-only methods at every compression ratio. The figure below shows the full comparison; the current analysis refines and extends only the SVD family.

NoteCadzow denoising with adaptive rank and imputation

F-X Cadzow: working frequency bin by frequency bin (parameters used: nw=64, f_max=100 Hz, max rank r=5, gap_threshold=2.0, ppca_k=2.0)

This is the F-X (frequency–space) variant of Cadzow denoising, borrowed from seismic processing. Rather than applying SVD to the full time × channel matrix, the algorithm works one frequency bin at a time:

  1. rfft the snippet → complex array \(W \in \mathbb{C}^{n_c \times n_f}\).
  2. For each frequency bin \(f \leq f_\text{max}\), extract the spatial vector \(w_f \in \mathbb{C}^{n_c}\) (one complex amplitude per channel).
  3. Build a block-Toeplitz trajectory matrix \(T_f\) from \(w_f\).
  4. Compute the rank-\(r\) SVD of \(T_f\), zero the remaining singular values, and read off the denoised amplitudes.
  5. irfft back to the time domain.

Outlier imputation (ppca_k): after the first rank-\(r\) projection, channels deviating by more than \(\text{median} + k \cdot \text{MAD}\) are replaced by their model prediction; the SVD is repeated on the cleaned data.

NoteGap-criterion rank selection (discarded)

We investigated an alternative rank-selection criterion based on the largest relative drop in the singular value spectrum (the “gap”):

\[r_\text{gap} = \underset{i}{\arg\max}\; \frac{s_i}{s_{i+1}} + 1\]

We also swept a gap threshold \(g\), defining rank as the last position where \(s_k / s_{k+1} \geq g\).

The figure reveals why this criterion was discarded: after Cadzow denoising, the SV ratio at rank 1 is only 1.3–2.4 across all 11 PIDs — the dominant “gap” is barely larger than the secondary gaps. There is no clean separation between signal and noise in the SV ratio spectrum, so the gap threshold has very little sensitivity to the compression ratio. The ε-threshold (noise-floor-relative) criterion is far better calibrated for this data.

## Overview

The IBL holds **936 hours** of Brainwide Map (BWM) recordings and **1472 hours** from the Ephys Atlas.
Raw LFP at 2500 Hz, 384 channels, float32 amounts to ~12 TB for the BWM alone.
After standard preprocessing (bad-channel rejection, 2–250 Hz bandpass, ×10 decimation to 250 Hz), the footprint shrinks to ~1.2 Tb — still too large for routine distribution or streaming.
The goal is to identify a lossy compression strategy that reduces this further.

**Practical recommendation: SVD-adapt-CR32-WP4.** Setting the SVD stage to CR≈32 (rank≈12, epsilon≈48) and WP keep_frac ≈ 0.25 gives a total CR≈128 with SNR > 10 dB.
**This would shrink the dataset to ~9.6 Gb.**


## Pre-processing pipeline

Raw LFP (NP1, 2500 Hz, `.cbin`) was preprocessed before benchmarking:

1. **Bad-channel detection** — channels with anomalous variance flagged and excluded.
2. **Bandpass + CAR + decimation** — 2–250 Hz FIR bandpass, common-average referencing, ×10 FIR decimation → 250 Hz float32.
3. **Cadzow PPCA spatial denoising** — F-X Cadzow on 3 s snippets (nw=64, f_max=100 Hz, max rank r=5, adaptive rank via singular-value gap threshold=2.0, PPCA outlier k=2.0) to remove incoherent channel noise.

All methods were benchmarked on the Cadzow-denoised snippets so residuals reflect compression loss, not pre-existing noise.

![Cadzow denoising for PID e8f9fba4. Three 3 s snippets (rows): original / denoised (adaptive rank) / difference (same colour scale).](figures/2026-06-06_cadzow_e8f9fba4-d151-4b00-bee7-447f0f3e752c.png)

## SVD-adapt-WP algorithm in detail

The two-stage algorithm operates on a snippet matrix $X \in \mathbb{R}^{n_c \times n_s}$ (channels × samples):

**Stage 1 — spatial compression (SVD)**

$$X \approx \hat{X}_1 = U_r \, \text{diag}(s_r) \, V_r^\top$$

where $U_r \in \mathbb{R}^{n_c \times r}$, $s_r \in \mathbb{R}^r$, $V_r^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times n_s}$ are the top-$r$ singular triplets.
The rank $r$ is chosen to achieve a target CR (e.g. CR=24 → $r \approx 12$).

**Stage 2 — temporal compression (wavelet packets)**

Each of the $r$ rows of $V_r^\top$ is independently compressed using db4 wavelet packet decomposition (level 5).
Only the top-$f$ fraction of coefficients by magnitude are retained, giving an overall:

$$\text{CR}_{\text{total}} = \frac{n_c \, n_s}{r(n_c + n_s)} \cdot \frac{1}{f}$$

**SVD-adapt (ε-sweep)** selects rank automatically using:

$$\sigma_0 = \text{median}(s_{\lfloor r/2 \rfloor + 1}, \ldots, s_r), \qquad r^* = \max\{k : s_k > \varepsilon \cdot \sigma_0\}$$

Here $\sigma_0$ is the noise-floor estimate (median of the lower half of the full singular value spectrum), and $\varepsilon$ is a dimensionless threshold — the minimum signal-to-noise-floor ratio $s_k / \sigma_0$ required to retain a component. Equivalently, $\varepsilon(r) = s_r / \sigma_0$ is the $\varepsilon$ that would select exactly rank $r$ (as shown in the calibration figure). Sweeping $\varepsilon$ from $10^4$ (keep only the dominant component) down to $10^{-1}$ (keep almost everything) traces out the full CR curve.

**Reconstruction** reverses the two stages: reconstruct each wavelet-compressed row, then reassemble $\hat{X} = U_r \, \text{diag}(s_r) \, \hat{V}_r^\top$.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Prior context: transform methods

Before focusing on SVD variants, we benchmarked six approaches: SVD, Wavelet Packets (WP), DCT, DCT-δ, STFT, and SVD+WP.
SVD consistently outperformed all transform-only methods at every compression ratio.
The figure below shows the full comparison; the current analysis refines and extends only the SVD family.

![Initial aggregate benchmark (11 PIDs) including all transform methods. SVD and SVD+WP dominate at every CR. DCT-δ is worst throughout.](figures/2026-06-06_compression_aggregate.png)

![Reconstruction gallery from initial benchmark — PID dab512bd. SVD retains spatial structure to CR=100; transform methods show block/stripe artefacts from CR=30.](figures/2026-06-06_compression_gallery_dab512bd-a02d-4c1f-8dbc-9155a163efc0.png)

![Residual gallery from initial benchmark. SVD/SVD+WP residuals are spatially incoherent; DCT and STFT residuals carry structured spectral artefacts at high CR.](figures/2026-06-06_compression_gallery_dab512bd-a02d-4c1f-8dbc-9155a163efc0_residual.png)
:::

## Cadzow denoising with adaptive rank and imputation

**F-X Cadzow: working frequency bin by frequency bin** *(parameters used: nw=64, f_max=100 Hz, max rank r=5, gap_threshold=2.0, ppca_k=2.0)*

This is the *F-X* (frequency–space) variant of Cadzow denoising, borrowed from seismic processing.
Rather than applying SVD to the full time × channel matrix, the algorithm works one frequency bin at a time:

1. **rfft** the snippet → complex array $W \in \mathbb{C}^{n_c \times n_f}$.
2. For each frequency bin $f \leq f_\text{max}$, extract the spatial vector $w_f \in \mathbb{C}^{n_c}$ (one complex amplitude per channel).
3. Build a **block-Toeplitz trajectory matrix** $T_f$ from $w_f$.
4. Compute the rank-$r$ SVD of $T_f$, zero the remaining singular values, and read off the denoised amplitudes.
5. **irfft** back to the time domain.

**Outlier imputation (`ppca_k`)**: after the first rank-$r$ projection, channels deviating by more than $\text{median} + k \cdot \text{MAD}$ are replaced by their model prediction; the SVD is repeated on the cleaned data.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Gap-criterion rank selection (discarded)

We investigated an alternative rank-selection criterion based on the largest relative drop in the singular value spectrum (the "gap"):

$$r_\text{gap} = \underset{i}{\arg\max}\; \frac{s_i}{s_{i+1}} + 1$$

We also swept a gap threshold $g$, defining rank as the last position where $s_k / s_{k+1} \geq g$.

![Gap ratio sv[k]/sv[k+1] at each rank boundary for each of the 11 PIDs. Reference lines at g=2, 5, 10.](figures/2026-06-10_gap_vs_rank.png)

The figure reveals why this criterion was discarded: after Cadzow denoising, the SV ratio at rank 1 is only **1.3–2.4** across all 11 PIDs — the dominant "gap" is barely larger than the secondary gaps.
There is no clean separation between signal and noise in the SV ratio spectrum, so the gap threshold has very little sensitivity to the compression ratio.
The ε-threshold (noise-floor-relative) criterion is far better calibrated for this data.
:::
